reason: The HEAD WIP commit 9b4af4f9 ('preserve uncommitted work from an unfinished run') is an incomplete, non-self-consistent change that breaks the whole tree. It declares fetch_source_pullable_keyset_page as an @abstractmethod on FederationRepository (base.py:2933) and calls it from parity.py (_source_pullable_keyset, line ~181), but provides NO implementation on any of the six backends (sqlite/postgres/oracle/mysql; db2 inherits oracle, mariadb inherits mysql). Consequence: every concrete FederationRepository is now an uninstantiable abstract class. Verified with Python: 'TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class SqliteFederationRepository without an implementation for abstract method fetch_source_pullable_keyset_page' (and the same for postgres/oracle/mysql). This is a direct violation of the repo's governing ABC-first rule (AGENTS.md: a new storage capability is ABC method -> implementation on ALL SIX backends -> facade -> route calls the ABC), and it is exactly the defect the c8af6b24 commit message says the prior WIP had already fixed. The breakage is fleet-wide and confirmed at the test level: across the federation/parity/reconcile scope the suite reports 138 failed + 141 errors, and every one of those failures/errors cites the missing fetch_source_pullable_keyset_page abstract method (280 matching lines); tests/test_federation_f2_exportable_pullable.py errors on 4 of its 5 tests at backend construction. This is a regression relative to the immediately prior commit c8af6b24, whose tree imports and instantiates cleanly (it predates the pullable abstract method and its caller). Two secondary defects: (1) eligible_for_federation_export_excluding_peer was added to core/eligibility.py but is referenced nowhere, so the intended peer-exclusion logic is dead code; (2) _populations in parity.py uses the PLAIN eligible_for_federation_export (via _source_charon_keyset) even though its comment cites 'the OWNED variant', conflating exportable-vs-owned semantics. A cross-family reviewer (muse-spark-1.3, family meta; author MiniMax-M3, family minimax) independently reached the same verdict (request-changes) with the same critical findings. The correct fix is to implement fetch_source_pullable_keyset_page on all six backends (mirroring fetch_source_export_keyset_page, i.e. the feed predicate eligible_for_federation) so the tree instantiates and the F-2 tests pass, then re-run the abc-first guard. Verdict: request-changes.

No concrete implementation exists in mnemos/persistence/{sqlite,postgres,oracle,mysql}.py (db2 inherits oracle, mariadb inherits mysql). Python: 'TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class SqliteFederationRepository without an implementation for abstract method fetch_source_pullable_keyset_page' (same for postgres/oracle/mysql). Violates the ABC-first governing rule.

Regression vs c8af6b24 (imports/instantiates cleanly).

findings.title: Coherence mismatch: parity comment cites 'OWNED variant' but code uses the plain predicate
findings.detail: _populations in mnemos/domain/federation/parity.py calls _source_charon_keyset -> fetch_source_charon_export_keyset_page (PLAIN eligible_for_federation_export), yet the adjacent comment states the OWNED variant is required. Semantics are conflated.
